On Wed, Aug 19, 2026 at 10:27 AM Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Thanks for the heads up and for including request ids. We’re opening an incident bridge now and our on-call infra team is triaging.

Initial findings from the bridge: we observed a correlated increase in memory pressure on a subset of GPU workers serving cobalt2b around 09:56–10:12 UTC. That triggered OOM-driven worker restarts and transient 5xx responses while autoscaler cycled replacements.

What we’ve done so far:
- Scoped affected pools and increased headroom (moved traffic away from hot pods).
- Enabled a short-term fallback route to cobalt2b-quant-v2 (light quantized variant) for traffic from ClearRoute to reduce pressure.
- Collected heapdumps and request trace bundles for the affected workers (attached).

Next steps:
- Karthik to run a trace-level memory allocation analysis and assess whether a params/cache bug contributed.
- Marissa to coordinate a controlled rollout of the quant fallback for remaining sessions and monitor error rates.

Alice — from your side, if you can delay a non-urgent burst and confirm retry settings we can keep error rate lower while we stabilize.

---
Ben Carter
On-Call Infrastructure Engineer — Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 19 Aug 2026 12:05:00 -0400
Subject: RE: Repeated 503s from cobalt2b since 09:58 UTC

Quick technical follow-up with early root hypotheses: after parsing the trace bundles, I see anomalous KV cache growth for short-sequence requests (pattern matches requests with repeated small prompts). A recently merged change to per-sequence caching introduced an edge-case where small prompts could cause incremental cache entries to not be pruned until full sequence completion; under sustained short-session traffic this can push memory usage high on workers with older kernel scheduling (some regions still on kernel v5.10).

Immediate mitigation we implemented at 11:10 UTC:
- Toggled per-sequence caching to a conservative LRU policy for cobalt2b workers on affected pools.
- Coordinated fallback routing to quant variant for ClearRoute traffic only.

I’ll continue a deeper mem-alloc review and open a follow-up ticket for the caching change revert + test coverage. Tentative RCA: interaction between caching change + kernel scheduling + particular traffic pattern.

Karthik
Senior Applied ML Engineer — Serving Runtime
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Date: Thu, 20 Aug 2026 16:45:00 -0400
Subject: Cobalt2b incident summary and next steps (postmortem attached)

Hi Alice —

Thanks again for raising the alert and for quick collaboration while we triaged. This is a short post-incident summary and action plan; the full postmortem PDF is attached.

Summary:
- Impact window: 2026-08-19 09:56 UTC — 2026-08-19 11:18 UTC (peak errors ~10–15% for ClearRoute traffic).
- Root cause (short): regression in per-sequence caching logic combined with worker-level memory pressure on older kernel hosts, causing OOM restarts and transient 5xx responses.

Actions taken during incident:
- Scoped and drained affected worker pools.
- Enabled conservative LRU caching and routed ClearRoute traffic to cobalt2b-quant-v2 while we stabilized.
- Collected heapdumps and request traces; attached for your review.

Follow-up action items (owner / ETA):
- Revert risky caching change and add unit/regression tests (Karthik / 2 business days).
- Upgrade kernel on remaining older hosts to v5.15 (Infra / 3 weeks) and add monitoring for unusual KV cache growth (Marissa / 1 week).
- Expand canary policies for caching changes to include short-sequence simulated traffic (SRE + Runtime / 1 week).

Compensation/credits: we will apply a small service credit for the impacted window to ClearRoute’s account and will confirm via billing. Naomi will follow up on the exact credit amount.

If you’d like a quick run-through of the postmortem and planned fixes, we can schedule a 30-minute call next week.

Best,
Marissa Cole
SRE Lead — Redwood Inference
